pattern.description: A real mouse drag selects the article text: starting at the section heading, the browser's blue selection highlight grows line by line down three bullets and into a fourth in under half a second, setting up the Chrome-extension capture ('I can just highlight what...').
pattern.why_premium: The highlight visibly marks the exact passage that becomes the insight, so the viewer tracks the cause-and-effect of the extension without callouts; the fast, continuous drag reads as fluent and confident.

build_hint.gsap: Recreate with per-line highlight bars: gsap.fromTo('.sel-line', {scaleX: 0, transformOrigin: 'left center'}, {scaleX: 1, duration: 0.06, ease: 'none', stagger: 0.03}) while gsap.to(cursor, {x: endX, y: endY, duration: 0.45, ease: 'power1.inOut'}) follows the leading edge.
build_hint.remotion: For line i, widthPct = interpolate(frame, [start + i*1, start + i*1 + 2], [0, 100], {extrapolateLeft: 'clamp', extrapolateRight: 'clamp'}); cursor y = interpolate(frame, [start, start + 14], [y0, y1], {easing: Easing.inOut(Easing.quad)}). No spring; linear sweep.

notes: Screen-recorded native text selection (not an authored animation). The selection briefly overshoots then trims at the end of the drag in the filmstrip; durations are guesses. No SFX candidates.
